partially_covered.missing: Organization lacks data properties for legal name, VAT ID, contact info, legal form, etc. Only address and identifier are present via role assignment.
Item lacks properties for description, product code, classification, brand, etc. Only linked via InvoiceLineItem.

No explicit SHACL constraint individuals or axioms for mandatory EDIFACT/D96A fields; SHACLConstraint class is present but not populated. Cardinality restrictions for invoice sections are present but not for technical validation.

cq_coverage.details: Core structure and relationships for invoices, roles, and amounts are well covered; partial coverage persists for organization/item details and validation logic. Minor improvements in organization attribute modeling.

strengths: EDIFACT hierarchy and procurement roles modeled with deep class structure
Functional properties and cardinality restrictions for key relations
weaknesses: No general class axioms (GCAs) or equivalence definitions for complex classes
Limited advanced property characteristics (no transitive/symmetric properties)
Technical vocabulary for EDIFACT segments/elements not expanded since last iteration

likely_oops_pitfalls: P7: Inverse properties present for most relations, coverage is good
reasoner_risks: Hermit/Pellet will succeed as only OWL 2 compliant datatypes are used
No advanced GCAs or complex restrictions that might cause DL failures

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add data properties to Organization (e.g., legalName, vatID, contactInfo, legalForm) and to Item (e.g., description, productCode, classificationCode, brand) to fully answer CQ5 and CQ8.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables complete answers for organizational and item details; improves semantic interoperability.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Define explicit SHACL constraint individuals and/or axioms for mandatory D96A/EDIFACT fields, logical consistency (e.g., price sums), and file format validity to fully support CQ13.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Supports robust automated validation and regulatory compliance.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add general class axioms (GCAs) and owl:equivalentClass definitions for Invoice, OrganizationRoleAssignment, and other pivotal classes.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Strengthens semantic rigor and supports advanced reasoning.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand EDIFACT segment/element classes, code mappings, and technical vocabulary to cover more message types, segment codes, and data element codes.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves technical coverage and supports integration with EDIFACT tooling.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model advanced property characteristics (transitive, symmetric) and temporal properties (e.g., validity periods for roles) where appropriate.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enriches expressiveness and supports more complex business queries.

suggestions_addressed: Annotations are now complete for all classes and properties
Minor enrichment of cardinality and functional properties for key relations
suggestions_ignored: No new data properties for Organization or Item (CQ5, CQ8)
No explicit SHACL constraint individuals or axioms (CQ13)
No technical vocabulary expansion for EDIFACT segments/elements
improvement_tracking.notes: Incremental improvements in annotation completeness and property characteristics, but major CQ and validation gaps remain unaddressed. Ontology is stable and reasoner-friendly but lacks depth in data modeling and technical vocabulary.

summary: The ontology remains robust for core EDIFACT invoice structure and procurement roles, with thorough annotations and well-defined relations. However, it continues to lack full support for organization and item details, and explicit validation logic. Quality and coverage have improved slightly, but most high-priority suggestions from the previous review are still outstanding. Further enrichment is needed for full semantic interoperability and regulatory compliance.
